<description>
Alternative approach to #36688, citing the relevant parts of its description:

[quoted text omitted]
Fix this by only adding a socket to the `select()` exception set while waiting for a non-blocking `connect()` to complete. Windows needs that to detect a failed connection. Established connections no longer monitor the exception set on any platform. This approach was suggested by theuni in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36716#issuecomment-6931290348 and replaces the earlier version of this PR, which ignored the exception set outside Windows and disconnected on it on Windows.

We could instead have set `SO_OOBINLINE` on our sockets, so `recv()` returns any urgent data sent to us (and likely leads us to disconnect the peer). RFC 6093 doesn't forbid this, but the current approach seems more clear and direct to me.

The PR makes one additional change for clarity: if `errorSet` is reported for a socket we did not request to read from, disconnect directly instead of first attempting a send that would fail (emits a different log message). `if (recvSet || errorSet)` is left as is. Since `select()` no longer reports errors for established connections, this only applies to `poll()`.

A new unit test in `sock_tests` covers the fix itself: with an urgent byte pending, waiting for `RecvEvent` must time out. Without the fix it fails on a `select()` build.

`p2p_socket_errors.py` checks that the node ignores a single urgent byte: the connection stays open, ordinary data is still processed and the urgent byte is not counted as received. It also covers a peer reset while the node is sending, for the `poll()` change above.

Backports until 29.x are straight-forward, but for 31.x and before require compensating for the scripted-diff in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/f395acdeeeaa1f3fd75d3cedbf2731fa24083e9f, for the log format change in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/22335474d768f99067856173ff2764b6db753f67. If we also want to backport to 29.x then the scripted diff for https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/fa9cf38ab666b50b0d8e82cb17f9e5a8a613547d and the infamous https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/9f36962b07eff2369577a17c8adeaa0433697e1c need to adjusted for.
</description>

[2026-11-23] c:7106944603 comment by theuni (member) (edited 2026-11-23):
[quoted text omitted]
I disagree with this framing. Yes, it was a winding road to get here, but the changes are straightforward:
- Disconnect if we didn't request a read, but we get a hup/error event. This prevents us from reading when we shouldn't because we're paused. Afaik this would be safe to add by itself.
- Registering for errors when using `select` is harmful in all but one case (detecting connection failures), and in that one it is required. Require callers to opt-in if they require this failure. For `poll`, this is a noop. This has the effect of disabling select "errors" that weren't really errors.

Otherwise, things stay the same. Draining for `poll`/`select` happens as before, but we avoid the harmful non-error "errors".  We could add a few harmless `#if[n]def USE_POLL` in the higher layers to demonstrate where the changes have effects if that would help?

As I mentioned above, the less hackish way of doing this would be to introduce a `WaitForNewConnection()` which would be straightforward as the only way to register for an error event when using `select`. I proposed the more hackish event flag here instead to avoid having to change the `Sock` class and its derivatives, and the tests/fuzzers to go with it. I don't think we can have it all here.. either a quick hack that is small and targeted and backportable, or a more correct fix that's more invasive.
